title: Recent Linux Improvements that Impact TCP Throughput: Insights from R&E Networks
problem: TCP throughput limitations constrain Data Transfer Node (DTN) performance in R&E networks. Kernel-level inefficiencies prevent full utilization of available network bandwidth.
motivation: High-throughput data transfer is critical for scientific computing in R&E networks, making kernel-level network optimizations essential for DTN systems.
method: The researchers tested two Linux kernel features designed to speed up data transfer: MSG_ZEROCOPY (which sends data directly from user memory to the network instead of copying it multiple times) and BIG TCP (which reduces overhead by allowing larger packets to be sent at once). They ran controlled experiments at AmLight and ESnet testbeds, comparing Linux versions 5.15 and 6.8 on Intel and AMD processors across various network conditions. They measured how much faster data could be transferred when combining MSG_ZEROCOPY with packet pacing (spacing packets over time) and BIG TCP optimizations.
key_novelty: Systematic real-world testing reveals how two Linux kernel optimizations—MSG_ZEROCOPY and BIG TCP—improve data transfer speeds, with effectiveness varying across different processors and network conditions.
contributions: MSG_ZEROCOPY with packet pacing achieves up to 35% throughput improvement
Linux 6.8 provides 38% WAN and 30% LAN throughput gains over Linux 5.15
Cross-processor analysis demonstrating kernel optimization effectiveness on Intel vs AMD
Production-ready DTN configuration recommendations based on testbed results
limitations: Paper does not discuss limitations regarding hardware scope or workload diversity beyond network throughput metrics.
